metadata.note: The Milwaukee Road's Wisconsin Valley Division - New Lisbon, Wisconsin Rapids, Junction City, Wausau, Merrill - and the North Woods Hiawatha that ran it. Wausau was one of the map's measured coverage holes, with no drawn passenger line within 200 km in any era, although the Wisconsin Valley Railroad had reached it in 1874 and the Milwaukee Road ran trains here until 1970. The layer is split at Wausau because the two halves lost their service fourteen years apart: the train was cut back to Wausau on April 29 1956, and the southern half carried on to 1970.
geometry_sources: Traced from OpenStreetMap route relations 5816813 (CN Valley Subdivision, the ex-Milwaukee Road Wisconsin Valley line) and 9420940 (UP Adams Subdivision, the ex-Milwaukee main line at New Lisbon), stitched into one graph, Dijkstra between terminals, Douglas-Peucker at 15 m.
not_yet_sourced: No North Woods Hiawatha timetable was found, so both avg_speed_kmh values and every headway_min in this file are estimates.

Merrill - Tomahawk - Minocqua - Star Lake, the northern 60-odd miles of the North Woods Hiawatha's route, is abandoned, absent from OSM and not drawn. The train's documented 187-mile length is therefore only about 118 miles on the map.

The original Wisconsin Valley Railroad ran from Tomah, not New Lisbon; the Tomah - New Lisbon end of the 1873-74 line is not drawn, and the 1874-1936 segment is drawn on the New Lisbon connection the Milwaukee Road used later.
The Chicago and North Western also served Wausau and is not drawn.
metadata.passenger_only_rule: Drawn to 1956 north of Wausau and 1970 south of it, when the Milwaukee Road's service ended. CN still runs freight over the whole line; that is not drawn.

properties.company: Chicago, Milwaukee, St. Paul and Pacific Railroad
properties.line: Milwaukee Road: Wisconsin Valley Division (New Lisbon – Wausau)
properties.speed_source: Estimated. No North Woods Hiawatha timetable was found; 70 km/h is a guess for a streamlined train making eight or nine stops in 92 miles, and the pre-1936 local trains were slower.

segments.note: Built by the Wisconsin Valley Railroad out of Tomah - construction began 1872, 45 miles were open to Wisconsin Rapids in 1873, and the line was completed to Wausau by way of Junction City in 1874, with Merrill beyond. The Milwaukee Road took it over and ran it as its Wisconsin Valley Division, connecting with the Chicago main line at New Lisbon - which is where this trace starts, rather than at Tomah where the original railroad did. headway_min is an unsourced estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the 1872 construction start, the 1873 opening to Wisconsin Rapids and the 1874 completion to Wausau via Junction City are from the Rip Track Wisconsin railroad timeline and the Tomahawk Area Historical Society; the Wisconsin Valley Division name and the New Lisbon connection are from the Wikipedia Wausau station article. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

segments.note: The North Woods Hiawatha, the first new route to take the Hiawatha name, ran from 1936 over the 187 miles from New Lisbon up the Wisconsin Valley through Babcock, Wisconsin Rapids, Junction City, Wausau, Merrill and Tomahawk to Minocqua and Star Lake. headway_min 1440 counts the one Hiawatha each way; local trains ran besides it.
sources: Segment-level: the 1936 start, the 187-mile New Lisbon - Star Lake route, the station list and the April 29 1956 end of the Hiawatha name are from the Wikipedia North Woods Hiawatha article and american-rails.com. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate - no timetable running time was found.

segments.note: On April 29 1956 the Hiawatha name was dropped and the train cut back to Wausau; unnamed local service over this southern half continued until the Milwaukee Road discontinued it altogether in 1970. Wausau - Merrill and everything north lost its passenger service in 1956 and is drawn as the separate northern feature in this file.
sources: Segment-level: the April 29 1956 name drop and cut-back to Wausau, and the 1970 discontinuance, are from the Wikipedia North Woods Hiawatha article and american-rails.com. headway_min is an estimate.

properties.geometry_quality: 92.3 traced miles New Lisbon - Wausau on the present-day CN Valley Subdivision, the ex-Milwaukee Road alignment, passing within 1.8 km of Babcock, Wisconsin Rapids and Junction City. No straight-line legs over 3.1 km. The North Woods Hiawatha's own documented length is 187 miles New Lisbon - Star Lake, of which this feature is the southern half and the Wausau - Merrill feature the next 26 miles; the rest, Merrill to Minocqua and Star Lake, is abandoned and not in OSM, so it is not drawn.
